The study reveals normal knee joint alignment, no definite fracture line detected.  
  
  There is deformed shape, hyperintense signal in almost entire of the ACL, with loss of femoral attached site.  PCL is intact. Mild anterior tibial translation is noted.   Mild bone marrow edema at posterior lateral and medial proximal tibia is observed.  
  
  MCL is intact.    Normal shape with preserved signal of medial meniscus is observed. 
   
   FCL, popliteus tendon, biceps femoris tendon are preserved.  
    Lateral meniscus is not torn. 
  
   No osteochondral lesion is detected.  
  
   Moderate amount of PF joint effusion with fluid distended suprapatellar bursa and mild thickened synovial tissue are observed.  The PF joint and joint surface are preserved.   
   The quadriceps and patellar tendons are preserved.   Complete tear of ACL  
   Post traumatic reactive PF synovitis with mild suprapatellar bursitis

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Gonalgia lateral izquierda.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Meniscos de morfología y señal conservada, sin criterios categóricos de rotura.
Cartílagos de los compartimentos femorotibiales y patelofemoral sin alteraciones. No hay
significativo derrame articular ni quistes poplíteos patológicos.
Tendones cuadricipital, la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites
normales. Aumento de señal del tercio proximal del tendón rotuliano, sin signos de rotura.
Edema las partes blandas, profundo a la región insercional de los tendones de la pata de ganso.
Edema las partes blandas de la banda iliotibial y el cóndilo femoral lateral.
Impresión:
Leve tendinosis rotuliana proximal.
Probables fenómenos de fricción de la banda iliotibial.
Probable bursitis laminar profundo a los tendones de la pata de ganso

MRI of left Knee with 
-3-Plane Loc, Sag PD FS, Cor T2 FS, Sag T2 FS, Sag T1, Screen Save, Ax T2 FS

Wearing of articular cartilage of patella and femoral condyle and subchondral edema and cysts in lateral face of patella and femoral trochlea and spur formation, in favor of osteoarthritis with grade 4 chondromalacia.  Spur formation and tiny cystic change over tibial intercondylar eminence
Suspicious of lateral tilting of patella
> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, without significant extending into the surface, in favor of  grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to degeneration. Mild bulging of medial and lateral meniscus
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
> Subcutaneous edema over anterior left knee.
> The contour of ACL  appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
    Mild interstitial incresed signal intensity of PCL on T1WI  and F/S T2WI, R/O degeneration or grade 1 injury.
    Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Thickening of iliotibial band, R/O tendinosis.
> A small bone island in left distal femur.
> Thickening of iliotibial band.
Impression: 
1. C/W osteoarthritis of left knee, with grade 4 chondromalacia of patellofemoral joint.
2. Synovitis of left knee and suprapaellar bursitis and patellar plicae.
3. R/O degeneration of meniscus.
4. R/O degeneration or grade 1 injury of PCL.
5. R/O tendinosis of iliotibial band.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

MRI LEFT KNEE  (plain)

Clinical information:
History of left knee giving out

Technique: 
Multiplanar MR of the knee according to protocol.

Comparison: 
None

Findings: 

Menisci

Lateral meniscus: No surfacing hyperintensity of the posterior horn is probably due to intrasubstance degeneration. No definite meniscal tear detected. No para meniscal cyst.

Medial meniscus: intact

Ligaments

Anterior cruciate ligament: Chronic complete tear with anterior tibial translation of approximately 1.0 cm.

Posterior cruciate ligament: intact but buckled from the anterior tibial translation.

Medial collateral ligament: Superficial and deep components intact. No periligamentous edema.

Lateral collateral ligament: The iliotibial band, biceps femoris tendon, fibular collateral ligament and popliteus muscle and tendon intact. 

Posterolateral corner structures: Intact

Extensor Mechanism

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patella is normally positioned within the femoral groove. There is no retinacular disruption.

Fluid

No joint effusion or loose body. Trace Baker's cyst.

Osseous and Articular Structures

Bones: No fracture, stress reaction, or osseous lesion is seen.

Patellofemoral compartment: Minimal chondrosis.

Medial compartment: Minimal chondrosis.

Lateral compartment: Up to severe chondral loss at the tibial plateau with chondral fissures and subchondral edema.

Others:

Hoffa's fat pad: clear

Muscles: No abnormal oedema. 

Neurovascular bundle: Normal 


COMMENT
Full-thickness chronic tear of the anterior cruciate ligament resulting in anterior tibial translation approximately 1 cm. Posterior cruciate ligament is intact but is buckled from the anterior tibial translation.

Up to severe chondrosis at the lateral tibiofemoral compartment with full-thickness chondral fissures and loss at the lateral tibial plateau associated subchondral edema.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Daño meniscal.
Hallazgos:

Rotura compleja con componente principal horizontal oblicuo del cuerno posterior y parte del

Aumento de señal del aspecto superoexterno de la grasa de Hoffa.

Rotura compleja del menisco medial, sin desplazamiento significativo de segmentos.

> Increased fat stranding and minimal fluid accumulation located along the pes anserinus, R/O Anserine bursitis
  Small Baker's cyst.
> Mild tendinosis of iliotibial band and quadriceps tendon.

Impression: 
1. Tear of medial meniscus with parameniscal cyst.
   Degeneration of lateral meniscus.
2. Tear of PCL.
3. Grade 2 injury of MCL.
4. Grade 1 injury of ACL and LCL.
5. Anserine bursitis.
6. Synovitis of right knee and suprapatellar bursitis and patellar plicae; small Baker's cyst and popliteus bursitis.
7. Subcutaneous edema over right knee.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation
